Curious Minds, Bright Futures
Hannah Williams Headteacher
Welcome to Monkston Primary School
Welcome to Monkston Primary School. We hope our website offers a clear insight into our welcoming, community-centred school with unwavering inclusive values, bold aspirations and rich experiences that enable every child to thrive. We support our pupils to build resilience, work collaboratively and develop a lifelong curiosity for learning.
Opened in 2001, Monkston provides an environment in which both pupils and staff are challenged to achieve their very best and are genuinely valued for their contributions. We are committed to delivering outstanding pastoral care alongside rich, engaging learning experiences, working in close partnership with parents and carers as children progress through the school.
I have been proud to work at Monkston for nearly 25 years and became Headteacher in 2017—the same year the school joined Kingsbridge Educational Trust. Many of our staff have also been part of the Monkston journey for a significant time, bringing a wealth of experience and a deep understanding of the priorities and expectations of our local community.
We offer an engaging and ambitious curriculum, enhanced by a broad range of enrichment opportunities. In our most recent Ofsted report, inspectors noted that “Pupils relish the challenges of the school’s interesting and varied curriculum. They enjoy learning and are particularly keen to take part in the wide range of trips, clubs and visits on offer.”

Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to Monkston Primary School. We hope our website offers a clear insight into our welcoming, inclusive community school, where integrity, compassion and respect are at the heart of everything we do. We support our pupils to build resilience, work collaboratively and develop a lifelong curiosity for learning.
Opened in 2001, Monkston provides an environment in which both pupils and staff are challenged to achieve their very best and are genuinely valued for their contributions. We are committed to delivering outstanding pastoral care alongside rich, engaging learning experiences, working in close partnership with parents and carers as children progress through the school.
I have been proud to work at Monkston for nearly 25 years and became Headteacher in 2017—the same year the school joined Kingsbridge Educational Trust. Many of our staff have also been part of the Monkston journey for a significant time, bringing a wealth of experience and a deep understanding of the priorities and expectations of our local community.
We offer an engaging and ambitious curriculum, enhanced by a broad range of enrichment opportunities. In our most recent Ofsted report, inspectors noted that “Pupils relish the challenges of the school’s interesting and varied curriculum. They enjoy learning and are particularly keen to take part in the wide range of trips, clubs and visits on offer.”
At Monkston, we take a ‘heart and soul’ approach to teaching and caring for children. We are driven by a genuine desire to make a positive and lasting difference, supporting pupils to grow into enthusiastic, thoughtful, compassionate and responsible UK and global citizens. In short, we aim to change the world.
If you are considering Monkston for your child and would like to find out more, or to arrange a visit to our nurturing and supportive school, please contact us or book a tour here
Hannah Williams Headteacher

Attendance & Absence
If all children at Monkston are to achieve well, make the most of their time at school and nurture their skills and future opportunities, then regular attendance and punctuality is key. Without this, learning is disrupted and irregular, leading to many children not being able to achieve their full potential. All staff and governors are committed to meeting Monkston’s obligations with regard to this by ensuring the following:
Monkston strongly urges parents/carers to avoid booking holidays during term time, as this significantly affects educational progress.
From September 1st 2013, changes were made to Government legislation regarding taking holidays during term time. Schools are now no longer able to authorise absence for family holidays. Absence for participation in sporting events, family events (e.g. weddings of a very close family member, religious celebrations, graduations etc.) and for compassionate reasons will be considered on an individual basis and may be authorised.
Parents/carers are asked to contact the school to report their child’s absence by 9:00am on the morning of the first day of absence by calling 01908 671034 or by email Further contact on each subsequent day of absence, as well as advising when they are expected to return, is expected. Where the school has not been contacted regarding an absence, the school will attempt to contact the parent/carer by phone, text or email. If there is no response and the school are concerned about the welfare of a child or family and have been unable to contact anyone from the contact list held, then the school may contact the police and request a welfare check for the family.
Monkston School expect every pupil’s attendance to be above 95%. Parents will be notified if attendance falls below 95%.
As part of our pledge to ensure outstanding attendance, we monitor pupil attendance every three weeks and identify any pupils who we believe may be at risk of harming their education due to their lack of attendance at school.
During these monitoring exercises, we do take into account individual extreme cases where pupils have had other circumstances or illnesses which has resulted in lower than expected attendance.

Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to Monkston Primary School. We hope our website offers a clear insight into our welcoming, inclusive community school, where integrity, compassion and respect are at the heart of everything we do. We support our pupils to build resilience, work collaboratively and develop a lifelong curiosity for learning.
Opened in 2001, Monkston provides an environment in which both pupils and staff are challenged to achieve their very best and are genuinely valued for their contributions. We are committed to delivering outstanding pastoral care alongside rich, engaging learning experiences, working in close partnership with parents and carers as children progress through the school.
I have been proud to work at Monkston for nearly 25 years and became Headteacher in 2017—the same year the school joined Kingsbridge Educational Trust. Many of our staff have also been part of the Monkston journey for a significant time, bringing a wealth of experience and a deep understanding of the priorities and expectations of our local community.
We offer an engaging and ambitious curriculum, enhanced by a broad range of enrichment opportunities. In our most recent Ofsted report, inspectors noted that “Pupils relish the challenges of the school’s interesting and varied curriculum. They enjoy learning and are particularly keen to take part in the wide range of trips, clubs and visits on offer.”
At Monkston, we take a ‘heart and soul’ approach to teaching and caring for children. We are driven by a genuine desire to make a positive and lasting difference, supporting pupils to grow into enthusiastic, thoughtful, compassionate and responsible UK and global citizens. In short, we aim to change the world.
If you are considering Monkston for your child and would like to find out more, or to arrange a visit to our nurturing and supportive school, please contact us or book a tour here
Hannah Williams Headteacher

PE and Sport Premium
At Monkston Primary School, we understand the importance of PE and endeavour to provide a balanced curriculum that allows children to develop their physical skills and maintain a healthy active lifestyle from reception to year 6. We hope to not only provide children with the physical skills and knowledge needed to participate in sports, but also to ensure children enjoy lessons and continue to keep active when they leave our school.
As well as leading weekly indoor and outdoor PE lessons, we offer the children additional opportunities to participate in sports in our enriched curriculum, which has been provided through the sports premium funding. This includes having an outside specialist coach coming into school and working with all pupils in Key Stage 2. Children who are selected to represent the school in cross country and athletics are then provided with weekly training sessions with the sports coach.
For break and lunch times, we have invested in two new football goals, so that children can play football during break and lunchtimes and keep active; we have updated lots of our other lunch time equipment this year, such as new balls, skipping ropes, hoops and balance balls, in the aim to encourage children to keep active during break times.

Young Carers
Monkston Primary was awarded a Bronze award in May 2023. The three year award is in recognition of the school’s work to ensure that pupils don’t miss out on an education because they are young carers.
The Young Carers in Schools programme helps primary and secondary schools improve outcomes for young carers and celebrates good practice through the Young Carers in Schools Award.
Identifying Young Carers at Monkston
Young carers at Monkston are identified through a family referral or by a class teacher. The referral is confidential and is in place to support the parent/carer and child to achieve their best.
To inform the school of a young carer, please email [email protected] with your name, name of the young carer and the best method of contact. Alternatively contact the school on 01908 and request a call back from one of the young carer’s team.
If your child’s class teacher completes a referral for your child, a member of the team will be in touch to discuss the referral before any action is taken.
Across Kingsbridge Education Trust, there has been a growing focus on supporting young carers to achieve their best in school and feel supported. This work began at Oakgrove Secondary School and is now filtering down to the primary schools in the Trust.
Our aim is to raise awareness of young carers, identify who might be in need of some extra support and work with families to provide this.
Who could be identified as a Young Carer?
A young carer is a young person aged 5 – 18 who looks after someone who can’t manage without help. For the young carer, this could mean looking after a parent, brother or sister, grandparent or family friend who has a disability, long term illness, or drug and alcohol related issues.
As many as one in 12 pupils could be a young carer, and unless the school is advised about a pupil’s home circumstances, young carers risk first being identified by negative aspects of their behaviour or work. Some young carers worry about bullying and may be tired, worried, find it difficult to concentrate and have limited time for friendships and activities after school. If this is the case, we can help.
How can the school help?
Monkston Primary can provide extra help for young carers by offering homework clubs, drop in sessions, mentoring support from a peer or teacher and other school issues that may arise. The school works with Young Carers MK in order to supplement its systems and provide a wider range of activities for young carers in the area.
Useful information and help
For more immediate support, young carers can text YM to 85258 in order to message crisis support at Young Minds or call Carers UK Support on 0808 808 7777.
